content.text: Both changed source files have been read in full. Analysis: **`lib/diary/month.ts`** — A pure calendar builder. Inputs: numeric year/month, a `today` date string, and typed `DayLog[]`. Output: a `Cell[]` array. There is no sink here — no shell, SQL, filesystem, network, HTML render, eval, or logging. `iso()` interpolates numbers into a date-key string; the Map key uses the log's `worn_on` for lookup only. Data flows out to a React caller as an ordinary data structure. No security-relevant behavior is introduced. **`components/closet/item-view.tsx`** — The only substantive change is wrapping the existing `` in a `{g.imageUrl && ...}` guard, plus adding `loading="lazy"`/`decoding="async"`. This is a defensive change that reduces attack surface (avoids `` re-fetching the page). No new sink is introduced — the `src=` binding, the `Link href={\`/closet/${g.id}\`}` template, and the alt text existed before this diff. `` does not execute `javascript:` URIs, and `data:text/html` is not rendered as HTML by ``, so even if `g.imageUrl` were attacker-controlled it doesn't yield XSS via this attribute. **Phase 2c checks**: - No observability sinks touched - No IaC / CI trust / allowlist / permission grants - No parser/validator introduced (the `g.imageUrl && ...` truthiness gate is a null-guard, not a security allowlist) - No control regression — the prior code had no validator to remove - No fail-open state — buildMonth is deterministic **Sibling parity**: The comment claims the same guard exists on the hero image and closet card; I verified the hero above (`{imageUrl && ...}` at line 115 of the same file) matches. Not a security-relevant gate anyway. No source→sink path with missing mitigation identified.
